name: Extreme cold and wind chill – Prairies and the North

geo.extent: Prairie provinces, northern BC, the territories, northern Ontario and Quebec

description: Interior and northern cities have long periods below −20 °C. In the 1991–2020 normals, nights below −20 °C average about 52 days a year at Winnipeg, 49 at Saskatoon, 45 at Regina, 103 at Yellowknife and 122 at Iqaluit, against about 2 at Toronto and none at Vancouver. In January 2024 temperatures fell into the minus 40s across the West (−48.4 °C at Puntzi Mountain, BC) and Alberta set its all-time power-demand record.

practical_implications: Heating cost and reliability; block heaters; frostbite risk with wind chill
Outdoor activity shifts to winter sports

sources.title: Canada's 10 most impactful weather stories of 2024

limitations: Normal-day counts come from the linked clim records (ECCC 1991–2020). Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
